campaign: V1 Phase B.0.7+ CDI persistence verification (Q9 additional empirical test)
purpose: Per Anil 2026-05-26 Q9 additional verification request: test that /etc/cdi/cipher.yaml survives nvidia-ctk regeneration cycles. Test conducted in /tmp/cdi-test/ to avoid sudo writes to /etc/cdi/; mechanism behavior is identical.

test_1_q9a_sibling_yaml_same_kind.description: Per Anil Q9 (a) spec verbatim: drop cipher.yaml with kind: nvidia.com/gpu + additional CIPHER mounts under devices[].all.containerEdits
test_1_q9a_sibling_yaml_same_kind.cipher_yaml_content:
cdiVersion: 0.5.0
kind: nvidia.com/gpu
devices:
  - name: all
    containerEdits:
      env: [CIPHER_TEST_PERSISTENCE=yes, CUDA_INJECTION64_PATH=/usr/lib/cipher/libcipher_rt.so]
      mounts: [{hostPath: /usr/lib/cipher/libcipher_rt.so, containerPath: /usr/lib/cipher/libcipher_rt.so, ...}]
test_1_q9a_sibling_yaml_same_kind.mechanism_finding: CDI rejects duplicate device declarations across spec files (same vendor+class+device_name = conflict). Per CDI design intent: each device declared by exactly ONE spec file. With both nvidia.yaml and cipher.yaml declaring nvidia.com/gpu=all, neither nvidia.com/gpu=all is registered; CDI only registers the non-conflicting per-device entries (nvidia.com/gpu=0 + nvidia.com/gpu=GPU-...). The customer's `--gpus all` flag would not find nvidia.com/gpu=all device, breaking GPU container startup entirely.
test_1_q9a_sibling_yaml_same_kind.implication_for_q9a: Q9 option (a) extend-nvidia.com/gpu-via-sibling-cipher.yaml is INFEASIBLE per CDI's collision-detection semantics.

test_2_cipher_com_gpu_kind_persistence.description: Alternative test: cipher.yaml uses NEW kind cipher.com/gpu (avoids the nvidia.com/gpu collision). Verify it survives nvidia-ctk cdi generate.

Generated CDI spec with version 1.0.0 (nvidia.yaml regenerated)
test_2_cipher_com_gpu_kind_persistence.persistence_verdict: PASS (md5 unchanged; nvidia-ctk only touches its target file nvidia.yaml; cipher.yaml at different kind survives intact)
test_2_cipher_com_gpu_kind_persistence.but_problem: cipher.com/gpu=all requires customer to add `--device cipher.com/gpu=all` to docker run command. Docker's `--gpus all` flag maps ONLY to nvidia.com/gpu device class. So cipher.com/gpu kind preserves persistence but violates Goal 5 verbatim (requires customer-side flag).

consolidated_branch_c_finding.verdict: BRANCH C mechanism finding per V1_PHASE_B_SCOPE_LOCK §8 (R-A.1-equivalent caveat: surface mechanism findings immediately, do NOT silently scope-degrade).
consolidated_branch_c_finding.summary: M1 nvidia-container-toolkit CDI mechanism is the correct meta-architecture for substrate injection. The WITHIN-M1 implementation path Anil 2026-05-26 Q9 (a) proposed (sibling cipher.yaml, same nvidia.com/gpu kind) FAILS at CDI collision-detection layer. Three alternative sub-paths within M1 need Anil adjudication before B.1'' amendment lands.

sub_P1_modify_nvidia_yaml_in_place.mechanism: cipher-platform .deb postinst patches /var/run/cdi/nvidia.yaml (or generates /etc/cdi/nvidia.yaml that takes precedence) to add CIPHER mounts + env to the existing nvidia.com/gpu=all entry's containerEdits. Customer's --gpus all triggers BOTH NVIDIA's libs AND CIPHER's libs through the SAME nvidia.com/gpu=all device.
sub_P1_modify_nvidia_yaml_in_place.fragility: MEDIUM - every NVIDIA driver update or nvidia-ctk auto-regenerate wipes CIPHER additions; postinst-upgrade-hook + repeat-on-driver-update needed
sub_P1_modify_nvidia_yaml_in_place.engineering_cost: ~2-3 ED (patch script + driver-update hook + .deb upgrade machinery)
sub_P1_modify_nvidia_yaml_in_place.recommendation: RECOMMENDED if Anil accepts the driver-update-time re-patch operational cost

sub_P2_take_over_etc_cdi_nvidia_yaml.mechanism: cipher-platform .deb postinst runs nvidia-ctk cdi generate to produce nvidia spec, ADDS CIPHER mounts, writes result to /etc/cdi/nvidia.yaml. /etc/cdi/ takes precedence over /var/run/cdi/ per spec-dirs order. CIPHER OWNS the /etc/cdi/nvidia.yaml file.
sub_P2_take_over_etc_cdi_nvidia_yaml.fragility: HIGHER - CIPHER becomes responsible for regenerating /etc/cdi/nvidia.yaml on every NVIDIA driver update; stale-spec risk if cipher-platform .deb is not updated in lockstep with driver
sub_P2_take_over_etc_cdi_nvidia_yaml.engineering_cost: ~3-4 ED (generation + merge tool + driver-version-tracking + upgrade machinery)
sub_P2_take_over_etc_cdi_nvidia_yaml.recommendation: STRONG long-term answer but heavier v1 lift

sub_P3_cipher_com_gpu_kind_plus_customer.mechanism: cipher.yaml uses kind cipher.com/gpu (cleanly coexists with NVIDIA's nvidia.com/gpu). Customer adds `--device cipher.com/gpu=all` to docker run.
sub_P3_cipher_com_gpu_kind_plus_customer.recommendation: REJECTED - violates Goal 5 verbatim per Anil 2026-05-26 contract correction

consolidated_branch_c_finding.additional_consideration: Open question: does newer Docker (29.x) or k8s offer auto-include-all-CDI-devices behavior (e.g., NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=all-cdi-vendors) that would let cipher.com/gpu=all auto-trigger alongside nvidia.com/gpu=all? Anil may want to investigate this OR conclude sub-P1 is the v1 answer. Pre-existing precedent: NVIDIA visible-devices env var has historically been NVIDIA-specific; cipher.com extension would require a new mechanism.
